answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a costly bond and earn trust through repeated, independently signed trades. Existing agents randomly challenge newcomers, checking answers against a juniper registry, a mirror record held by unrelated peers, and a relic of prior behavior. Inconsistent identities are slashed and denied credit. A sybil attacker must fund every fake account, then risk losing each bond when coordinated fraud is exposed, so multiplying identities becomes expensive.
